---
title: "Agent skills"
---

OMERO-Screen ships **agent skills**: instructions that teach an AI agent
(Claude, or another coding agent) how to use OMERO-Screen. With them installed,
you describe what you want in plain words. The agent runs the commands, checks
the results and tells you what it did. It asks before it changes anything in
OMERO.

The skills cover three things:

| | What the agent does for you |
|---|---|
| **Analyse** | Loads single-cell data from CellView, runs the analysis, and makes the cell-cycle, feature and intensity plots used in our papers. |
| **Images** | Opens plates in napari, collects example cells, trains and tests a cell classifier, and renders galleries and whole-well images that show what the numbers say. |
| **Tracks** | Reviews tracked cells in napari together with you. It moves the viewer to each cell, shows a filmstrip, and proposes fixes to a lineage that you confirm or reject. Every decision goes into one edit log, so it can be audited and undone. |

There are three skills behind this:

- **omero-screen**: the pipeline, CellView, plots, napari and images.
- **cellclass-train**: classifier training from your labelled cells to a finished model.
- **track-review**: reviewing cell tracks with a human in napari.

The [Skills](../skills.html) page shows every file of each skill.

## Install

You need OMERO-Screen installed first ([Install & configure](installation.qmd)).

### Claude (desktop app or Claude Code)

- **Claude Code** (terminal, or the desktop app's **Code** tab): the skills come
  as one **Claude plugin** from our marketplace:

  ```
  /plugin marketplace add HocheggerLab/omero-screen
  /plugin install omero-screen@omero-screen
  ```

- **Claude desktop app (chat):** the app does not read plugin marketplaces.
  Download each skill as a zip and drag it into the app's window for adding a
  skill:

  - [omero-screen.zip](../downloads/omero-screen.zip)
  - [cellclass-train.zip](../downloads/cellclass-train.zip)
  - [track-review.zip](../downloads/track-review.zip)

  The full walkthrough is in [Working with Claude](claude.qmd).

#### Keeping the skills up to date

We publish improved skills with each OMERO-Screen release.

- **Claude Code:** automatic updates are **off** for marketplaces outside
  Anthropic's own. Turn them on once: run `/plugin`, open **Marketplaces**,
  select **omero-screen** and switch on auto-update. Or update by hand:

  ```
  /plugin marketplace update omero-screen
  /reload-plugins
  ```

  A running session keeps the old skills until `/reload-plugins` or a new
  session.
- **Desktop app:** download the zips again and replace the skills.

### Other agents

The skills follow the open [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format, so
other agents can use them too. We ran our evaluation of agent-driven analysis
with the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent.

- **With npx** (Node.js needed). This lists the three skills and asks which
  agents to install them for:

  ```bash
  npx skills add HocheggerLab/omero-screen
  ```

- **By hand.** Copy (or link) the skill folders from
  [`plugins/omero-screen/skills/`](https://github.com/HocheggerLab/omero-screen/tree/main/plugins/omero-screen/skills)
  into your agent's skills folder: `~/.pi/agent/skills/` for Pi,
  `~/.claude/skills/` for Claude Code.

## Connect napari (for track review)

Track review needs the agent to see and drive your napari window. The GUI
install includes our fork of [napari-mcp](https://github.com/HocheggerLab/napari-mcp),
which lets OMERO-Screen add its review tools to the agent's toolbox.

1. Start napari and open **Plugins → napari-mcp → Start Server**. It listens
   on `http://127.0.0.1:9999/mcp`.
2. Open the **Track Review** widget and load your review queue.
3. Register the server with your agent once. For Claude Code:

   ```bash
   claude mcp add --transport http napari-review http://127.0.0.1:9999/mcp
   ```

   Other agents that support MCP servers over HTTP use the same address.

4. Start a **new** agent session. The tools are listed when the session
   connects, so napari must be running first.

The details, including what an agent may change on its own, are in
[Reviewing tracks](../tracking/review.qmd#working-with-an-agent).

## Things to ask

Say what you want in your own words. The agent asks when it needs a plate
number or a channel name.

**Analyse**

> Analyse plate 1234. This is a cell-cycle and DNA damage analysis after siRNA
> depletion of genes X, Y and Z. Make a PowerPoint with a lab-meeting style
> summary of the data.

You get a slide deck with the cell-cycle and DNA damage plots per siRNA, the
numbers behind them and a short summary of what changes, plus the Python code
that made the plots, so every figure can be regenerated.

**Images**

> Show me the cells the micronucleus classifier calls positive in wells B3 and
> C3 of plate 1234, next to the control.

You get galleries of the classified cells for each well, saved as image files,
with a manifest recording which cells and settings were used.

**Classifier**

> Train a classifier on the cells I collected and show me how well it does.

The agent builds the dataset, runs the standard training sweep and gives you a
report with accuracy, a confusion matrix and the best model, ready to publish
to OMERO.

**Tracks**

> Load the review queue in napari and go through the open cells with me.

The agent shows each cell in your napari window, explains what looks wrong,
for example a broken track or a false division, and proposes the fix. You
confirm or reject it in the widget.

> Make a movie of cell 234 showing its FUCCI intensities over time and its
> cell-cycle phases as it moves through G1, S, G2 and M. Save it to the
> Desktop.

You get a video file on your Desktop: the cell followed through the
timelapse, with its FUCCI traces drawn alongside and each frame labelled with
its phase.

## Good to know

- **The agent asks before changing OMERO**: running the pipeline, publishing a
  classifier, deleting anything. It reads and plots without asking.
- **Your password never goes into the chat.** `omero-screen setup` saves it
  in a file only you can read.
- **The agent works on your computer.** napari opens windows on your screen,
  and OMERO is reached over your network, so use an agent that runs locally
  (Claude Code, the Code tab of the Claude desktop app, or Pi).
